final_decision.semantic_equivalence_basis: For the supplied four-rank, N=7000 benchmark, the process grid is 4x1 and every rank owns 1750x7000 cells. Each rank enters runSimulation and immediately launches computeFluxKernel using locally initialized energy and materials. Communication occurs only after this first numerical update. In particular, non-root rank 3 owns the bottom corners with nonzero external flows, so its first kernel performs useful numerical work independently of rank 0. It can execute that work after returning from the initial barrier but before rank 0 records its start. Later halo communication cannot retroactively enclose that work. Although the stop boundary establishes completed work globally, the root's interval is therefore not a proven global makespan.
final_decision.notes: Reviewed the actual benchmark configuration: four hybrid ranks, -n 7000 -i 4000. No validation-specific timing dispatch changes this conclusion. No missing device synchronization, timer-unit error, or timing-datatype mismatch is present.
